A multi-narrator Victorian novel: five single-narrator sections (the drawing-master's two chapters, the solicitor's, the elder sister's diary, the uncle's narrative). Names renamed (see PROVENANCE.md).
author: Wilkie Collins
source: Project Gutenberg #583 (public domain, US; PG wrapper stripped)
synopsis: Walking back to London after midnight, the young drawing-master Edwin Calloway meets a frightened woman dressed all in white who has escaped from an asylum. Next day he takes up a post at Thornholm House in Fellshire, teaching the half-sisters Harriet Lisle and Clara Wendover under the roof of Clara's reclusive, hypochondriac uncle Lionel Wendover, and finds that Clara bears an uncanny likeness to the fugitive of the night road, Ellen Pryor. Edwin and Clara fall in love, but she is promised to the baronet Sir Roderick Ashby, and Edwin leaves England. The family solicitor Matthew Hollins cannot protect Clara's fortune in the marriage settlement. At Greymere Park in Southmarch, Harriet's diary records Roderick's debts and temper and the arrival of his friend, the vast, charming and formidable Count Morandi, with his wife, Clara's aunt; Roderick, deep in debt, demands Clara's signature on a deed he refuses to explain, and the Count persuades him to put it off. Ellen Pryor, who knows Roderick's secret, dies in London and is buried under Clara's name, while Clara is shut in the asylum as Ellen. Harriet frees her sister. Edwin, returned, sets out to prove Clara alive: he uncovers the forged parish register that hides Roderick's illegitimacy, Roderick dies in the burning vestry, and Edwin forces Morandi to write a confession before the Count flees and is killed abroad. Edwin and Clara marry, and Clara's identity is restored at Thornholm.
